claim: Disinflation in the general IPC proves that the purchasing power of poor households has recovered.
estimand: Real disposable command of low-income households over their specific basic basket
public_language: Disinflation is relevant, but purchasing-power recovery must be measured against the basket and disposable resources of the affected households.

claim: Stable aggregate employment implies stable job quality.
estimand: Composition and quality of employment, including formality, hours, earnings and stability
public_language: Stable employment does not establish stable quality; composition, hours, formality and earnings must be shown.

claim: The registered-worker count represents the total employment situation.
estimand: Total employment across registered and unregistered forms
public_language: Registered employment is an administrative perimeter, not the total labor market.

claim: The total wage index measures the income trajectory of all workers and households.
estimand: Distribution of real labor and household income across employment forms
public_language: Wage indices are not universal household-income indices; coverage and distribution matter.

claim: 'Economic activity is growing' is a horizon-invariant statement.
estimand: Growth across original year-on-year, seasonally adjusted monthly, trend-cycle and cumulative horizons
public_language: Activity must be stated with horizon: August was down year-on-year, marginally up month-on-month and flat in trend.

claim: The September fiscal result is unambiguously either surplus or deficit.
estimand: A result with fixed institutional perimeter, accounting basis, period and treatment of intra-public flows
public_language: September can show a cash surplus for the SPN and an accrual deficit for the APN without contradiction; perimeter and basis must be named.

claim: The accumulated fiscal surplus proves structural fiscal strength.
estimand: A recurrent, comprehensive and sustainable fiscal balance after extraordinary items, omitted accruals and fiscal risks
public_language: The surplus is an observed result; calling it structural requires stripping extraordinary items and incorporating omitted obligations and fiscal risks.

claim: Bank-family delinquency measures total household financial stress.
estimand: Total household debt stress across banks, non-bank providers, informal borrowing, arrears and ability to pay
public_language: Bank mora is a formal-system indicator, not a census of household financial stress.

claim: Credit growth proves an improvement in household welfare.
estimand: Whether new credit increases productive capacity/consumption smoothing or finances distress and refinancing
public_language: More credit can be useful or distress-driven; balances alone do not identify welfare.
